title: Clarinet solo style in the old days
summary: He took high-register solos and played chords behind the band; he thinks most New Orleans clarinetists played alike.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: In those days, did the clarinetists play mostly in the upper register? Sometimes low register solos? Or how did they do it nowadays? They'd maybe take a whole chorus in the low register and then they'd take another chorus in the high? Yeah. How did you play in those days?

Well, I'd play my, I'd play, in those days I'd play my solos in the high register. I had a system, I had a system of my own that when I'd take solo, most of the time they'd let the clarinetists take two chords. Well, I'd play the melody, the first chords and then get off on the second. On the variations then?
Yeah. With the band, did you usually just play like chords and arpeggios up and down or other counter melody, more like another melody with it or more of the chords most of the time?
No, most of the chords. The chords, mm-hmm.

Did most of the clarinet players play that style or some of them maybe use more runs than others or are there many different styles on the clarinet or would you say most of the New Orleans fellas used about the same style?
It seems to me most of them played about the same style.
